sections.title: Supply Chain Analytics Market Size
sections.body: Supply chain analytics is the smallest market in this dataset at $11B+, growing 25% year over year, with 2,748+ adopting organizations, one of the largest vendor fields reviewed at roughly 89,700 products, and 9M+ professionals. The extreme vendor-to-revenue ratio marks a young, crowded analytics layer evolving on top of enterprise systems. Buyers should anchor on integration with existing ERP and logistics platforms, since that determines whether the analytics layer delivers value or stays decorative. In practice, the $11B market against roughly 89,700 products means many vendors sell thin analytics layers — integration depth with ERP and logistics systems should be the first question in every demo, not the last. Despite the $11B market being the smallest reviewed, its 25% growth and 82% buyer intent make it a priority investment — integration quality with the 9M-professional ERP base is the differentiator vendors must prove.

sections.title: Adoption & Usage
sections.body: Supply chain analytics adoption is 79% among enterprises and a strong 69% among SMBs, with a high 82% planning to increase investment and a lean three tools on average. The broad adoption with strong intent signals a category in definite expansion — supply-chain stress has pushed analytics spend across firm sizes. Buyers should expect the gapless, low-tool setup to evolve toward dedicated platforms as demand-visibility requirements grow. The 82% intent is among the highest reviewed — expect the lean three-tool setup to expand toward dedicated demand-planning platforms as visibility requirements outgrow spreadsheet layers.

sections.title: ROI & Business Impact
sections.body: Supply chain analytics delivers a 332% average 12-month ROI with a 23% productivity improvement, a 19% cost reduction, and positive ROI in about four months. The strong return against modest operational percentages reflects the strategy value — visibility into demand and inventory that avoids stockouts and write-downs far outweighs the labor saved. Buyers should measure returns on inventory turns and forecast accuracy, since supply-chain value scales with those numbers. The 332% return against modest operational percentages shows the value sits in avoided stockouts and write-downs — finance teams should score ROI on inventory turns, not labor savings.

sections.title: Key Trends
sections.body: Nine trends shape supply chain analytics in 2026, led by AI integration in supply-chain platforms at 83% adoption, cloud-native deployments at 79%, and mobile-first solutions at 64%. Demand forecasting, inventory optimization, supplier-risk scoring, logistics telemetry analytics, and control-tower visibility complete the set, with data-quality governance spanning all nine. At 83% AI with 79% cloud-native, this is one of the most advanced trend profiles reviewed — expect control-tower visibility to become a table-stakes feature through 2026. sections.title: Budget Allocation
sections.body: Supply chain analytics budgets are a modest $127K per year at enterprises, $45K in mid-market, and $4K for small businesses — with the highest mid-market-to-enterprise ratio reviewed. The strong mid-market figure ties directly to the 82% investment intent and broad SMB adoption, as mid-size shippers and manufacturers fund visibility tooling. Buyers should expect this small, fast category to grow into its ambition, with demand-planning analytics the first budget line to expand. The highest mid-market-to-enterprise ratio reviewed — $45K versus $127K — confirms small shippers and manufacturers are funding visibility tooling; that is the demand engine behind the category's growth.
